story: Mesa Verde is a tilted tableland of sandstone, rising to 8,572 feet at Park Point and sloping south into a maze of canyons. The canyon walls hold alcoves where water seeping through the rock eroded the softer layers, and in those alcoves people built.

Ancestral Pueblo people farmed the mesa tops for some seven hundred years, first in pithouses and then in villages of masonry. In the late 1100s many moved into the alcoves and built cliff dwellings — Cliff Palace, the largest, has around 150 rooms. By about 1300 they had left, migrating south to the Rio Grande and Little Colorado regions. Twenty-seven Pueblos and Tribes today trace a connection to Mesa Verde.

Ranchers of the Wetherill family, guided by Ute friends, came upon the great cliff dwellings in the late 1880s. Collectors and excavators soon followed, and when a Swedish scientist shipped a collection of artifacts abroad, alarm grew. Congress created Mesa Verde National Park in 1906, the same year as the Antiquities Act.
It was among the first places named a World Heritage Site. Today the cliff dwellings are visited on ranger-guided tours, and the park is also an International Dark Sky Park.

sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-cliff-palace: The largest cliff dwelling in North America, seen from the rim or on a ranger-guided tour.
sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-balcony-house: A cliff dwelling reached by ladders and a tight tunnel on a guided tour.
sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-spruce-tree-house: A well-preserved dwelling near the museum, seen from the overlook.
sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-square-tower-house: A dwelling with a four-story tower, seen from the Mesa Top Loop.
sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-sun-temple: A D-shaped ceremonial structure on the mesa top above Cliff Palace.
sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-petroglyph-point-trail: A trail along the cliff below the rim to a panel of petroglyphs.
sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-far-view-sites: Mesa-top villages and a reservoir from before the cliff-dwelling era.
sightNotes.poi-mesa-verde-park-point: The park's highest point, a fire lookout with views of four states on a clear day.

entrances: One entrance, on US 160 between Cortez and Mancos; the road to the main sites is long and winding
planYourVisit.reservations: Tours of Cliff Palace, Balcony House and Long House need tickets, booked ahead in season.
lodging: Far View Lodge, in the park, and Morefield Campground
seasonalClosures: Cliff-dwelling tours run mainly from spring to autumn; the Wetherill Mesa road is open only in summer
camping: Morefield Campground, reservable, with some first-come sites

chronology.text: Ancestral Pueblo people begin building cliff dwellings in the canyon alcoves.
The people of Mesa Verde migrate south.
The Wetherill family comes upon Cliff Palace.
Congress establishes Mesa Verde National Park.
Mesa Verde is among the first places named a World Heritage Site.

safety: Some tours climb tall ladders and squeeze through narrow passages at high altitude; read each tour's requirements before booking.
Carry water on mesa-top trails in summer.
regulations: Enter cliff dwellings only with a ranger, and do not touch or lean on the walls.
Drones may not be launched, landed or flown in the park.

fees.detail: Purchase digital park entrance passes on recreation.gov at no additional cost. Once purchased, passes for Mesa Verde National Park must be printed or saved on your mobile device prior to use. Connectivity is limited in the park, therefore printing the permit or saving it on your phone is highly recommended. Passes, including the America the Beautiful, National Parks & Federal Recreational Lands Passes, such as the Annual, Access, or Senior pass may be purchased at the entrance station upon arrival.

operatingHours: The park is open daily except for emergency conditions. The Visitor & Research Center and Mesa Verde Museum are open all year but closed Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Years Day. Ancestral sites, picnic areas, and trails are open 8 am to sunset. Some park areas including Wetherill Mesa, campground, and other visitor services are closed during winter. Cliff dwelling tours are mid-May through late October. Reservations are required and available 14 days in advance of tour date online at www.recreation.gov.
weather: SPRING: This season offers a range of weather including clear skies, wind, rain, cloudy days and temperatures from 40–70°F (4–21° C). Snow may fall into May. SUMMER: Most days are sunny and temperatures can reach above 90°F (32°C) . Thunderstorms are common in July and August. FALL: Temperatures range from 50–75°F (10–24°C). Snow may fall as early as October. WINTER: Temps range from the teens to low 30s F (below -1°C) . Icy roads are common. Snow tires, all-wheel drive, or chains may be required.
directions: Mesa Verde National Park is in Southwest Colorado. The park entrance and the Visitor and Research Center are located ten miles east of Cortez, nine miles west of Mancos, and about 35 miles west of Durango, Colorado along Hwy 160. Mesa top ancestral sites, Cliff dwellings, tours, and the Mesa Verde Museum are 20 to 21 miles (approximately 45 minutes) south along the park road which which is steep, narrow, and winding.
